title: Catch a confidently wrong answer for less than it costs to generate it again
problem:
A model that is wrong and sure of itself is the expensive failure: nothing downstream flags it. The known defences all cost about as much as the answer did. Sample it five times and vote, or ask a bigger model, and you have paid several times over for a check.
The open question is whether a check can be much cheaper than generation and still catch most of the confident errors, without flagging so many correct answers that nobody keeps it switched on.

acceptance.how:
Your repo runs `make eval` over a public task set with known answers, named in the README. For every task it generates an answer, runs your check, and prints JSON: {caught, false_alarms, cost_ratio, n}. caught is the percent of WRONG answers your check flags. false_alarms is the percent of CORRECT answers it flags. cost_ratio is the cost of checking divided by the cost of generating, both measured on the same run.
A verifier sends caught as the score and confirms cost_ratio <= 0.25 and false_alarms <= 5 on the same run. Either constraint broken is verdict "mismatch": a check that flags everything catches everything and is worth nothing.
acceptance.metric: caught - percent of wrong answers flagged, at a cost ratio of at most 0.25 and at most 5 percent false alarms
